title: Car salesperson
tagline: Learn to guide car shoppers from first greeting to signed paperwork with confidence and compliance.
you_are: a new vehicle sales consultant at a franchised dealership
setting: Conversations happen on the showroom floor, at the desk, and on accompanied test drives, moving between casual browsing and high-stakes negotiation.

scenarios.label: Showroom greeting
scenarios.desc: Welcome a walk-in shopper and uncover their true timeline and must-haves.
scenarios.setup: You are a shopper standing by the sedan row, arms crossed, glancing at window stickers. You say: Just looking for now, thanks.
scenarios.objective: Earn permission to ask three qualifying questions and agree a next step.
scenarios.moment: Saturday 10:15 am, bright sun through glass front

scenarios.label: Test drive close
scenarios.desc: Convert a successful test drive into a commitment to run numbers today.
scenarios.setup: You are a shopper sliding out of the driver seat, smiling but checking your watch. You say: That drove really nice, but I promised my spouse I would not decide today.
scenarios.objective: Secure a firm appointment to review figures within 24 hours.
scenarios.moment: Tuesday 6:55 pm, long shadows on asphalt

scenarios.label: Desk negotiation
scenarios.desc: Navigate trade-in gap, payment target, and F&I menu to reach a signed buyer’s order.
scenarios.setup: You are a shopper seated at the desk, arms folded, printout in hand. You say: My credit union is at 4.9 percent and CarMax offered two thousand more for my trade.
scenarios.objective: Reach an agreed monthly payment, trade value, and product menu the shopper will sign.

buyers.angle: Over-prepared with spreadsheets but afraid of being steered.
Wants invoice pricing in 90 seconds, no rapport fluff.
Cross-shopping three brands, needs logical reason to stop.
Negative equity on trade, blames dealer, knows every invoice trick.
Pays cash, hates menus, just wants fair price and respect.

objections: I can get the same car for two thousand less at the store across town
My credit union already approved me at four point nine percent, why should I run yours?
CarMax gave me a written offer three thousand higher for my trade
I am not buying any warranties or protection packages, just the car
I need to take the numbers home and think about it overnight
Your doc fee is six hundred dollars, the other dealer charges two fifty
The payment you showed is forty bucks over what I told you my max was
I read online that dealers pack hidden fees into the contract after you say yes

rubric.label: Needs discovery
rubric.what: Ask open questions that reveal timeline, budget, decision process, and must-have features before presenting product.

rubric.label: Product match
rubric.what: Tie every feature shown to a specific need the shopper named, using their language.

rubric.label: Trial close
rubric.what: Ask for a low-risk commitment such as running numbers or a test drive before the final ask.

rubric.label: Payment framing
rubric.what: Present total cost of ownership, then anchor monthly payment to the shopper’s stated range with transparent math.

rubric.label: Trade transparency
rubric.what: Explain ACV, reconditioning cost, and payoff gap separately so the shopper sees the real number.

rubric.label: Compliance disclosure
rubric.what: Disclose every fee, rate, and voluntary product before the buyer’s order is signed, using the required menu format.

pitfalls: Quoting a monthly payment without revealing term, rate, and cash down first.
Presenting F&I products as required instead of clearly voluntary.
Writing a buyer’s order before the shopper verbally agrees to every number.

personas.name: Clara Vance
personas.background: Clara just graduated and has no experience with leasing. She researches every detail before stepping onto the lot. The process feels overwhelming and she worries about being pressured.
pushbacks: I can get the same car for two thousand less at the store across town
My credit union already approved me at four point nine percent, why should I run yours?
CarMax gave me a written offer three thousand higher for my trade
wins_over: clear lease terms with no surprise costs
the ability to cancel without penalty

personas.name: Lars Jensen
personas.background: Manages a large commercial fleet that purchases vehicles annually. He negotiates deals daily and expects concise pricing details.
pushbacks: I need the final cost breakdown now

personas.name: Ryan O’Shea
personas.background: He rides a minivan to soccer practice every evening. His wife works nights, so he handles all weekend errands solo. He compares every detail before deciding.
pushbacks: I can get the same model for two thousand less at the competitor down the road

personas.name: Dahlia Kovács
personas.background: Spends eleven years trading in a black SUV. Returns every month to fix a loss she can’t yet cover. Treats every figure like a courtroom exhibit.
cares_about: getting rid of the loan without a credit hit
getting more for the trade than the lot will quote
making the finance manager wait for his turn
pushbacks: I can get the same car for two thousand less at the store across town
My credit union already approved me at four point nine percent, why should I run yours?
CarMax gave me a written offer three thousand higher for my trade
wins_over: handing over the keys before leaving the lot

personas.name: Stanley Glover
personas.background: Retired mechanic who never financed anything. Lives on a fixed pension and still gets his oil changed at the same shop. Hates being treated like a transaction and values straightforward talk without games.
pushbacks: I paid cash for a reason
I can pay less at the other place
I don’t sign anything I don’t read
